title: Chronicle ingest orchestrator for lossless ordering and correlation stitching
creator: Nora Singh
description: Motivation: production incidents over the past two quarters revealed that partially-ordered log batches and aggressive client-side batching cause correlation IDs and span links to be lost or misordered during high-throughput bursts. Goal: deliver a streaming ingest orchestrator (Chronicle) that guarantees lossless ordering within tenant shards, attaches stable correlation anchors, and provides a transparent migration path from the current best-effort pipeline to an ordered, replayable flow that integrates with Loki/ELK backends. Scope: streaming adapter, shard key determinism, short-term durable staging, reordering buffer with bounded memory, schema normalization, schema-registry integration for structured fields, lightweight dedupe, and an ops-facing reprocessor for backfills. Excludes long-term cold storage and full-text reindexing (handled by separate work).
acceptance_criteria: Chronicle can receive structured JSON events and guarantee in-order delivery per tenant-shard under synthetic load (10k events/s per shard) without loss
Correlation anchors (corr_id) are persisted and included in Loki ingests and can be used to join traces in the trace UI
End-to-end latency from edge to Loki ingestion increases by less than 15% at p95 for normal load and stays within SLO for bursts via bounded buffering
Automated migration tool can run a 1-day tenant backfill using the orchestrator with a <2% duplicate rate and idempotent writes
Operational dashboards show reordering buffer occupancy, hot-shard signals, per-tenant drain status, and estimated backlog time
plan: Week 1: Design review and schema evolution contract with data-platform; finalize shard key (tenant_id + low-entropy selector) and contract for corr_id propagation
Week 2-3: Implement streaming adaptor and deterministic shard assignment; add local write-ahead staging and bounded reorder buffer
Week 4: Integrate schema normalization module and schema-registry client; implement dedupe heuristics based on event fingerprint
Week 5: End-to-end test harness (synthetic generator, trace joiner, Loki sink); run chaos tests for partial failures and restarts
Week 6: Canary rollout to <5% tenants, monitor dashboards and adjust buffer sizing/policy
Week 7: Backfill tool and docs; run a 24h tenant backfill in staging; complete runbook and handoff to oncall
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unbounded memory during massive spikes. Mitigation: enforce soft+hard limits and spill to ephemeral SSD with backpressure to clients.
Risk: Schema drift causing downstream parsing failures. Mitigation: strict schema-registry checks with fallback mapping and a quarantined error sink for manual review.
Risk: Increased p99 latency for small tenants. Mitigation: adaptive buffer sizing by tenant load and priority routing for latency-sensitive tenants.
Risk: Duplicates during backfill. Mitigation: idempotent write keys and dedupe fingerprinting, include backfill marker metadata
